title: How Walking Through Doorways Wipes Your Memory
description:
At the University of Notre Dame, psychologists asked volunteers to carry colored wooden blocks inside closed shoeboxes from table to table. Walking across one large room caused a twenty-three percent memory error rate, while walking the exact same distance through an open doorway raised errors to twenty-eight percent.

Brain scans and single-neuron recordings show that crossing a doorway fires boundary cells in the hippocampus to archive the last room while clearing the front working-memory desk. Walking back through a second doorway triggered another reset instead of restoring recall.

Research: Radvansky, Krawietz and Tamplin, University of Notre Dame (2011), Baldassano et al. (2017), and Zheng et al. (2022).
pinned_comment: When you blank in the kitchen doorway, do you retrace your steps or stand still until it clicks?
